deep.reconstruction:
This is the opening of a draft or outline of 'Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen' (published 1872). It contains no computations. It has an introduction plan and the start of §1.

(A) Einleitung (outline of the eventual Vorwort):
- Origin in the Zürich lectures of autumn 1858.
- The 'Kernpunkt' (the cut idea) recognised on 24 Nov 1858.
- A conversation with Durège on 30 Nov 1858.
- The idea was occasionally presented at the start of differential calculus courses.
- A talk at the 'Wissenschaftlicher Verein' in Braunschweig on 11 Jan 1864.
- Publication of this 'Gelegenheitsschrift' was finally prompted by Heine's 'Elemente der Functionenlehre' (Crelle 74, 1872), with a planned remark on 'my view of Heine's presentation'.

(B) §1, Properties of the rationals Q:
- Their foundation is set aside. Dedekind stresses that the rationals are a 'free (?)' creation of man and the necessary consequence of counting. Counting is itself the creation of the positive integers. The question mark on 'freie' marks hesitation; the published text says 'notwendige oder wenigstens natürliche Folge', and the phrase 'freie Schöpfungen' returns in 1888.
- I. Q is an ordered one-dimensional domain. For a ≠ b, a > b (equivalently b < a) iff a − b > 0. Transitivity: a > b and b > c imply a > c. In that case b is said to lie between a and c.
  - Implicit step (mine): a − c = (a − b) + (b − c), a sum of positives, hence positive.
- II. Density: if a ≠ c, there are infinitely many rationals b between a and c. A proof ('Bew.') was begun and struck out.
  - Implicit proof (mine): for a < c, b_n = a + (c − a)/n, n = 2, 3, …, are pairwise distinct and satisfy a < b_n < c.

The next page continues with intervals (a,c), the notion of 'Stück', and property V: each rational a splits Q into classes A1 and A2 with every a2 > every a1. That is the published property III, which leads to the cut.
errors: No mathematical errors. The order is defined via positivity of a − b; transitivity and density are stated without proof (the proof of II is struck through). 'Ausdruck: b liegt zwischen a und c' is attached to the case a > b > c only implicitly; this is fine. The question mark after 'freie' is Dedekind's own hesitation, not an error.

results.what: Chronology of the discovery of the cut idea: Zürich autumn 1858, key insight 24 Nov 1858, talk with Durège 30 Nov 1858, Braunschweig talk 11 Jan 1864, publication prompted by Heine 1872
results.usually_credited_to: Dedekind (Vorwort to Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen, 1872); the Durège and 1864 details are from Nachlass studies (e.g. Dugac 1976)

results.what: Rationals as a (free?) creation of the human mind, a necessary consequence of counting, which creates the positive integers
results.modern_name: Dedekind's constructivist/logicist view of number ('freie Schöpfungen des menschlichen Geistes')

results.what: Order on Q via positivity of the difference; transitivity; betweenness
results.modern_name: Q as an ordered field / linear order

results.what: Between two distinct rationals lie infinitely many rationals

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of the well-known 1872 essay; its contents and chronology match the published preface and §1. The only mildly notable details are the explicit 30 Nov 1858 Durège conversation, the 11 Jan 1864 Braunschweig lecture and the hesitant 'freie (?)'. These are already known from Nachlass scholarship (Dugac and others).

checkable.asserts: a−c = (a−b)+(b−c), giving transitivity of > from positivity of sums
b_n = a+(c−a)/n exceeds a by (c−a)/n > 0 when c > a, n ≥ 2
c − b_n = (c−a)(n−1)/n > 0 for n ≥ 2, so the b_n lie strictly between a and c
b_n ≠ b_m for n ≠ m when a ≠ c, so infinitely many rationals lie between a and c

transcription_corrections: 'ein eingeordnetes [?] Gebiet' should most likely read 'ein wohlgeordnetes Gebiet von einer Dimension', matching the published §1 ('ein wohlgeordnetes … Gebiet von einer Dimension'); this is not 'well-ordered' in Cantor's sense.
The struck word at the end is '[-Bew.-]' (start of 'Beweis'), followed by dots.
'Functionen-lehre' refers to Heine, 'Die Elemente der Functionenlehre', J. reine angew. Math. 74 (1872).
